proposal.title: Implement Aurelia-compatible video ROMs and Apple-format FlexiDisk II transfer
proposal.reason: Use the existing card ROM and dual-format disk-controller records. No additional display RAM, undisclosed accelerator or transparent legacy-program conversion is assumed. Full parity concerns the June 1979 Aurelia release, matching monitors and logical API behaviour. ROM sizing, host keyboard mappings and qualification remain explicit. Apple DOS 3.2 is the period target; later DOS 3.3 is not backdated.

chapters.description: This Apple II card uses slot decoding and a driver ROM while preserving the native memory map and avoiding conflicts with other cards. Native 6502 drivers, callable libraries and examples expose a card API; existing graphics are not transparently redirected, and no CP/M port or Z80 CPU is supplied.

The card reuses {display_controller_id} with {video_ram_kib} KiB of local display RAM from {video_chip_count} {video_chip_id} chips. Windowed or addressed host access leaves display refresh independent and does not add general-purpose host RAM. Two {sprite_chip_id} chips provide an exclusive 1 KiB, 8-bit sprite bus.

All five sprites remain available in supported Aurelia-family modes through a host-specific upload interface. The card has no Aurelia system DMA controller. chapters.description: Native MOS 6502 ROM firmware and libraries expose the common Aurelia TUI and graphics API without CP/M or a Z80 CPU. Apple-native graphics, sound and peripherals remain accessible through separate target libraries. Existing programs that bypass the API are not transparently redirected. Preserve the host memory map, qualify address decoding and wait states, and avoid conflicts with other installed cards.

The card reuses {display_controller_id} with {video_ram_kib} KiB of local display RAM from {video_chip_count} {video_chip_id} chips. Windowed or addressed host access leaves display refresh independent and does not add general-purpose host RAM. Two {sprite_chip_id} chips provide an exclusive 1 KiB, 8-bit sprite bus.

All five sprites remain available in supported Aurelia-family modes through a host-specific upload interface. The card has no Aurelia system DMA controller. Output uses {video_link_id}; 80-column output requires a compatible 640-pixel monitor, and all modes need card/monitor qualification. Host CPU performance limits drawing throughput. No monitor or FlexiBUS ports are included.

At the 4 June 1979 launch, the ROM and callable libraries implement every TUI feature and graphics mode of the contemporary Aurelia release: the same control semantics, text frames/windows, editing, clipping, glyphs, colours, display-mode behaviour and sprite services on matching qualified monitors. This is functional/API equivalence, not Z80 binary compatibility or equal drawing speed. Application state, clipboard buffers and control descriptors occupy bounded host RAM; complex controls can use linked helpers over ROM primitives. Logical keyboard commands use documented host mappings and menu equivalents where physical keys differ. Later pointer, professional-video and multitasking features are not implied.

Use the slot page as discovery and call entry points, with banked firmware behind the shared expansion-ROM window. A fixed RAM-resident trampoline restores card selection and bank state around disk or other peripheral calls, then returns safely to the correct ROM. Reserve zero-page and stack workspace and keep callbacks, interrupts and reentrancy within the published ABI. Determine ROM chip capacity/population from the linked firmware image; no additional memory is inferred from the existing supplied-set quantity.

chapters.description: This external drive uses {media} media and connects over {connection}. It handles {disk_formats} disk formats and is usable from {supported_hosts}.

For AION C 2.0, Aurelia writes native Apple II executables to Apple DOS 3.2-compatible 13-sector diskettes through this drive. The launch format uses 35 tracks, 13 sectors per track and 256-byte sectors. The local controller implements Apple-compatible GCR encoding/decoding, sector addressing, checksums and format/read/write operations; the Aurelia export utility maintains catalogue, free-space allocation and binary-file load-address/length headers. A raw sector copy without a valid filesystem and executable header is not a runnable application disk.

Move the completed diskette to a compatible Apple Disk II drive and load/run the binary under an existing Apple DOS 3.2 installation. This media-transfer route requires no Logix interface on the Apple. Alternatively, connect FlexiDisk II to the Apple through the Logix Apple II Expansion Card and its qualified disk-service adapter. Neither route runs CP/M on the Apple. Formatting a data disk does not supply or install Apple DOS; the developer uses an existing compatible boot disk. Later DOS 3.3 formats require a separately qualified update.

chapters.description: Native MOS 6502 ROM firmware and libraries expose the common Aurelia TUI and graphics API without CP/M or a Z80 CPU. Apple-native graphics, sound and peripherals remain accessible through separate target libraries. Existing programs that bypass the API are not transparently redirected. Preserve the host memory map, qualify address decoding and wait states, and avoid conflicts with other installed cards.

The card reuses {display_controller_id} with {video_ram_kib} KiB of local display RAM from {video_chip_count} {video_chip_id} chips. Windowed or addressed host access leaves display refresh independent and does not add general-purpose host RAM. Two {sprite_chip_id} chips provide an exclusive 1 KiB, 8-bit sprite bus.

All five sprites remain available in supported Aurelia-family modes through a host-specific upload interface. The card has no Aurelia system DMA controller. Output uses {video_link_id}; 80-column output requires a compatible 640-pixel monitor, and all modes need card/monitor qualification. Host CPU performance limits drawing throughput. No monitor or FlexiBUS ports are included.

At the 4 June 1979 launch, the ROM and callable libraries implement every TUI feature and graphics mode of the contemporary Aurelia release: the same control semantics, text frames/windows, editing, clipping, glyphs, colours, display-mode behaviour and sprite services on matching qualified monitors. This is functional/API equivalence, not Z80 binary compatibility or equal drawing speed. Application state, clipboard buffers and control descriptors occupy bounded host RAM; complex controls can use linked helpers over ROM primitives. Logical keyboard commands use documented host mappings and menu equivalents where physical keys differ. Later pointer, professional-video and multitasking features are not implied.

Use the slot page as discovery and call entry points, with banked firmware behind the shared expansion-ROM window. A fixed RAM-resident trampoline restores card selection and bank state around disk or other peripheral calls, then returns safely to the correct ROM. Reserve zero-page and stack workspace and keep callbacks, interrupts and reentrancy within the published ABI. Determine ROM chip capacity/population from the linked firmware image; no additional memory is inferred from the existing supplied-set quantity.

chapters.description: This external drive uses {media} media and connects over {connection}. It handles {disk_formats} disk formats and is usable from {supported_hosts}.

For AION C 2.0, Aurelia writes native Apple II executables to Apple DOS 3.2-compatible 13-sector diskettes through this drive. The launch format uses 35 tracks, 13 sectors per track and 256-byte sectors. The local controller implements Apple-compatible GCR encoding/decoding, sector addressing, checksums and format/read/write operations; the Aurelia export utility maintains catalogue, free-space allocation and binary-file load-address/length headers. A raw sector copy without a valid filesystem and executable header is not a runnable application disk.

Move the completed diskette to a compatible Apple Disk II drive and load/run the binary under an existing Apple DOS 3.2 installation. This media-transfer route requires no Logix interface on the Apple. Alternatively, connect FlexiDisk II to the Apple through the Logix Apple II Expansion Card and its qualified disk-service adapter. Neither route runs CP/M on the Apple. Formatting a data disk does not supply or install Apple DOS; the developer uses an existing compatible boot disk. Later DOS 3.3 formats require a separately qualified update.
